issues.claim: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/fundamentals/object-oriented/ (cited for encapsulation and the claim that a constructor check always runs)
issues.problem: The excerpt covers the definition of encapsulation and lists constructors as members. It says nothing about the cited claims: constructor validation always runs, an `init` accessor runs after the constructor in an object initializer, or a get-only property can be assigned only in the constructor. No cited link supports these claims.
issues.suggestedFix: Add or replace with sources that support them: the C# `init` keyword docs (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/keywords/init) and the properties or constructors docs. Keep the overview page only for the encapsulation claim.

issues.problem: The title is paraphrased. The fetched page is titled 'Classes, structs, and records' (heading 'Overview of object oriented techniques in C#'). The EN title also differs from the page.

issues.problem: Unnatural grammar: 'которого' is the wrong form here.
issues.suggestedFix: Его читает только валидатор, который кто-то должен запустить: `Validator.ValidateObject` или проверка модели в ASP.NET Core.

issues.problem: The excerpt covers separation of concerns, encapsulation, dependency inversion and explicit dependencies. It does not show interface segregation, Liskov substitution, role interfaces or splitting fat interfaces. It does not support the specific claims it is cited for.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace it with a source that supports the claims, or cite it only for the 'depend on abstractions and keep contracts stable' point. Also add a source for the Liskov claim, e.g. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liskov_substitution_principle or the .NET design guidelines. The ISP Wikipedia page does not mention substitutability.

issues.claim: Even `NotSupportedException` for an intentionally unsupported operation remains a sign of a poor contract unless the contract lets the caller check the capability up front, as `ICollection<T>.IsReadOnly` does.
issues.problem: The NotImplementedException excerpt is cut off before the NotSupportedException remarks, so the 'intentionally unsupported' wording cannot be confirmed from it. The `IsReadOnly` example is not backed by any cited link.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a link to the NotSupportedException or ICollection<T>.IsReadOnly API page, or soften the sentence to what the NotImplementedException remarks state.
